text:
Buffalo closed its road trip Sunday with a 6-2 win in Tampa, and it came with a nice footnote: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen's 100th career win, as Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report noted. It also capped a 3-6-1 stretch, and it leaves the Sabres right where their numbers say they belong. They are 10-10-4, with 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) and an even 50% share at 5v5. Our playoff race gives them a 24% chance, with a projection around 86 points.

The good news is up front. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have been Lindy Ruff's best trio: 59% of the expected goals in 129 minutes together, and a 9-4 edge in goals. Jiri Kulich has found his footing on the top line beside Tage Thompson, which the Buffalo News has written about at length.

The worry is the net and the penalty box. Alex Lyon has been the most written-about Sabre for the wrong reasons, with a string of losses that ended in Saturday's 4-3 defeat in Florida. The team has allowed 2.56 more goals than its chances predict, and it takes 4.08 penalties a game, more than it draws.

It doesn't help that Devon Levi, traded to Edmonton on July 1, has won 10 of his first 11 games as an Oiler. What to watch after the Thanksgiving break: whether Luukkonen's night starts a run in the crease, because the skaters have been good enough to stay in this race.
headline: A rout in Tampa for a .500 team
